issue_context.title: Device class for temperature sensors are missing
issue_context.body:
### The problem

Device class for temperature sensors is missing.

### What is version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2021.9.0b1

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

core-2021.8.8

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Container

### Integration causing the issue

octoprint

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/octoprint/

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
WARNING (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.sensor] Entity sensor.octoprint_target_bed_temp (<class 'homeassistant.components.octoprint.sensor.OctoPrintSensor'>) with device_class None reports a temperature in °C which will be converted to °F. Temperature conversion for entities without correct device_class is deprecated and will be removed from Home Assistant Core 2022.3.
```


### Additional information

_No response_

review_comments: Would be nice to use `entity_description` for these. As well as for `name` and `unit`.
Are all temperature sensors from octoprint measurements, or does it also expose aggregate values like min/max/average that are not considered a measurement?
They are all measurements, there are no min/max/average temperature readings in octoprint.
Feels like these would be simpler and less error-prone if `SENSOR_TYPES[octo_type]` was a dictionary, not a list
I saw PR that's going to revamp this if I recall and add a config flow, this is just to resolve the error in the reported issue.

Looks like you mean https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/46432. Looks like it's quite old and actually deals with older version of this integration that doesn't have crazy `SENSOR_TYPES` structure.
Anyway, it should be fine to land this PR as is but would be great if you could refactor it later.
> Feels like these would be simpler and less error-prone if `SENSOR_TYPES[octo_type]` was a dictionary, not a list
Agreed, I try to chunk these up into small PRs when possible.
New approach is to use `SensorEntityDescription` to structure possible sensors
Should I stuff that into this PR as well?
Let's do it in a new one.
